name: Canada Privacy Pack
description: DLP detection for Canadian personal information under PIPEDA, Quebec Law 25 and provincial health privacy laws such as Ontario PHIPA: Social Insurance Numbers, provincial health card numbers (Ontario, Quebec, British Columbia), passport and driver's licence numbers (Ontario, Quebec), with English and French labels, plus a low-confidence bank transit and account engine. All rules ship DISABLED at INFO severity (Zscaler's delivery convention): review, tune, then enable each rule and raise its severity.
deploy_note: Install one channel at a time. Deploy Web DLP first, check it, then Endpoint DLP, then SaaS, then Email, one channel per run. A small run is easy to verify and avoids the burst of requests that makes ZIA block the API client (Resource Access Blocked).
references: PIPEDA, Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (S.C. 2000, c. 5)
Quebec Law 25, Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information
Ontario PHIPA, Personal Health Information Protection Act, 2004
audience: Canadian organisations, and organisations holding Canadian residents' personal or health information, including health care providers and their vendors.
when_to_use: The customer operates in Canada or holds personal information of people in Canada, or the compliance profile is PIPEDA, Quebec Law 25 or PHIPA.
notes: No ZIA predefined dictionary for Canadian identifiers was confirmed in this repository (the banking pack carries a custom SIN pattern and says to prefer a predefined one when licensed), so every dictionary here is custom (assumed: check the tenant's predefined list and swap in predefined ones where licensed).

A ZIA pattern cannot run the SIN Luhn check, so each identifier needs a label (English or French) within 50 bytes and plain nine or ten digit numbers in prose do not fire. A SIN-shaped number that fails Luhn but sits beside a label still fires; the test file checks Luhn on its samples only.

Formats: Ontario health card is ten digits plus an optional two-letter version code; Quebec RAMQ is four letters plus eight digits (birth year, month with 50 added for women, day); British Columbia PHN is ten digits starting with 9 (its check digit is not validated: assumed). Ontario driver's licence is a letter plus 14 digits; Quebec is a letter plus 12 digits (A1234-123456-12; assumed: the Quebec digits are not validated). Other provinces' health cards and licences are not included.
The bank engine is low confidence: a transit or institution number AND an account number, each beside a label. Keep it in monitor mode.
Bilingual labels include accented and unaccented French spellings; add a customer's own wording before enabling.
